CC 3/2011 OF THE SPECIAL COURT (SPE/CBI), THIRUVANANTHAPURAM APPLICANT/APPELLANT/ACCUSED:
 N.GANESHAN, AGED 58 YEARS,
 S/O. R. NEELAKANDAIYER,
 RESIDING AT HOUSE NO.54, PREM NAGAR,
 KILLIPALAM, THIRUVANANTHAPURAM- 695002.

RESPONDENT/RESPONDENT/COMPLAINANT:
 CENTRAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION  REP. BY SPECIAL PUBLIC PROSECUTOR,
 HIGH COURT OF KERALA, ERNAKULAM- 682031.

Application praying that in the circumstances stated therein the High Court be pleased to stay the conviction passed in C.C.No.3/2021 by the Special Judge's Court (SPE/CBI), Thiruvananthapuram pending disposal of the appeal, in the interest of justice.

This Application coming on for orders upon perusing the application and this court's order dated 22.01.2019 in Crl.M.A.1/2019 in Crl.A.102/2019 and upon hearing the arguments of M/S.K.K.VIJAYAN,
SRI.K.R.RAJESHKUMAR, SRI.G.RANJU MOHAN, Advocates for the petitioner and of the ASSISTANT SOLICITOR GENERAL OF INDIA for the respondent
The appellant is the petitioner.
He seeks to stay the conviction.

2. The petitioner was convicted for the offences punishable under Section 120B read with Sections 409, 420 and 477 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and under Sections 13(1)(c) and (d) read N.Ganeshan vs Central Bureau Of Investigation on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190462572/
1 with Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (PC Act).

entities.text: N.Ganeshan vs Central Bureau Of Investigation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the appeal, execution of the sentence was suspended by this Court as per the order dated 22.01.2019.

The petitioner would contend that he is an International Umpire under the International Table Tennis Federation (the learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is an International Umpire under the the Table Tennis Federation of India) and he is the sole breadwinner of his family.
He received a show cause notice from the Federation, which may result in termination of his service as Umpire.
Hence, he seeks to issue an order staying conviction, failing which he would be put to irreparable loss and future.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Standing Counsel for the CBI.
4. The Apex Court in State of Maharashtra through CBI, Anti-Corruption Branch, Mumbai v.
Balakrishna Dattatrya Kumbhar

entities.text:
CBI, Anti-Corruption Branch, Mumbai v.
Balakrishna Dattatrya Kumbhar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: [ (2012) 12 SCC 384] enumerated the circumstances in which and parameters for staying conviction under the PC Act.

It was held:
"12.

Thus, in view of the aforesaid discussion, a clear picture emerges to the effect that, the Appellate Court in an exceptional case, may put the conviction in abeyance along with the sentence, but such power must be exercised with great circumspection and caution, for the purpose of which, the applicant must satisfy the Court as regards the evil that is likely to befall him, if the said conviction is not suspended.

The Court has to consider all the facts as are pleaded by the applicant, in a judicious manner and examined whether the facts and circumstances involved in the case are such, that they warrant such a course of action by it.
The court additionally, must record in writing, its reasons for granting such relief.
Relief of staying the order of conviction cannot be granted only on the ground that an employee may lose his job, if the same is not done."
5. In Afjal Ansari v. State of U.P. [(2024) 2 SCC 187]

entities.text: Afjal Ansari v. State of U.P. [(2024) 2 SCC 187]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the Apex Court dilated further the said proposition and observed that in a case where continued operation of conviction would lead to irreparable damage and the damage could not be compensated in monetary terms, that falls within the category of exceptional cases.

It was held that there is no gainsaying that in order to suspend the conviction of an individual, the primary factors that are to be looked into, would be the peculiar facts and circumstances of that specific case, where the failure to stay such a conviction would lead to injustice or irreversible consequences.

The very notion of irreversible consequences is centered on factors, including the individual's criminal antecedents, the gravity of the offence, and its wider social impact, while simultaneously considering the facts and circumstances of the case.
6. The petitioner is aged 64 years now.
Being an International Umpire, he may be able to pursue the assignments despite the age.
It is seen that on account of the conviction, disciplinary action was initiated against the petitioner and the result would be that he would not be able to involve in such activities.
Going by the aforementioned principles of law, loss of job or employment by itself is not a reason for staying the conviction.
There is no allegation of criminal antecedents against the petitioner.
The offences for which he is convicted is certainly serious.
It is to be noted that the petitioner acting as an Umpire would not any way affect interest of the general public.

Considering N.Ganeshan vs Central Bureau Of Investigation on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190462572/
2 the age of the petitioner, the nature of avocation to which he may be put in, it has to be said that the consequences that arises as a sequel to the conviction would be irreversible.

entities.text: N.Ganeshan vs Central Bureau Of Investigation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Although, ordinarily in a case of conviction for the offence under the PC Act there cannot be a stay of conviction,
considering the aforementioned circumstances, more particularly the innocuous nature of the engagement the petitioner may be put in, I am inclined to stay the order of conviction.

7. In order to see that the petitioner does not involve in any kind of undesirable and prohibited activities not only in personal life, but also in professional life as a condition for staying the conviction, the petitioner shall enter into a bond for Rs.5,00,000/- (Rupees five lakhs only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the Special Court.
It is made clear that any complaint of violation of the above conditions by the petitioner will result in cancellation of the order of stay as well as forfeiture of the bond to the Government.

List on 14.10.2025.
Sd/-
P.G. AJITHKUMAR, JUDGE dkr 11-04-2025 /True Copy/
